slides.title: Half-Close Connection
slides.body:
Introduction
A half-close occurs when one side finishes sending its data and closes its sending direction, while the other side's sending direction remains open. This is a valid operation in TCP

slides.title: Half-Close Connection
slides.body:
Key Point
The 4-way teardown studied earlier is essentially two independent half-closes happening one after the other — first the client’s half-close, then the server’s half-close

slides.title: Special Cases in TCP
slides.body:
Simultaneous Open and Close
Both sides send SYN at the same time, enter SYN_SENT, then move to SYN_RECEIVED after receiving SYN, and finally reach ESTABLISHED
Simultaneous Open

slides.title: Special Cases in TCP
slides.body:
Simultaneous Open and Close
 It uses 4 segments instead of the normal 3 because both sides pass through SYN_SENT → SYN_RECEIVED → ESTABLISHED after sending SYN simultaneously
 This occurs mainly in peer-to-peer systems where both sides know each other's IP and port
Simultaneous Open

slides.title: Special Cases in TCP
slides.body:
Simultaneous Open and Close
Both sides send FIN simultaneously → both enter FIN_WAIT_1
Both receive the other's FIN → send ACK → both enter CLOSING
Both receive ACK → TIME_WAIT → CLOSED
Simultaneous Close

slides.title: Simultaneous Close
slides.body:
Key Observation
In simultaneous close, both sides go through TIME_WAIT and the CLOSING state, unlike normal teardown
